findings.text: follow-on: the fragment states the base arm is tests/remote at 887486007, but the retained log header names revision b47967a65 and command tests/remote/test_executor.py tests/remote/test_remote_environment.py tests/remote/test_ssh_worker.py, so the base-green claim is not tied to the revision the fragment names.

follow-on: the fragment says the live fail measure shows bare python3 3.5.6 below the 3.12 floor, but /tmp/jt60sa-toolsenv-live-fail.log shows an interpreter not probed with Command 'probe_environment.py' returned non-zero exit status 1, so the live arm exercises the probe transport error, not the below-floor verdict the unit test covers.

follow-on: the fragment quotes EXIT=1 (and EXIT=0 at line 88) as part of the command output, but the retained live logs /tmp/jt60sa-toolsenv-live-pass.log and /tmp/jt60sa-toolsenv-live-fail.log contain no EXIT= line, so both exit codes are asserted rather than shown.

follow-on: tools status calls check_all_tools, which probes the remote environment at imas_codex/remote/tools.py:703, and get_python_status, which probes again at imas_codex/remote/python.py:266, so one invocation opens two environment probes and the CLI renders only the python_status result.

item_verdicts.diff: read base 887486007d862b2a920b71c02c7138e821929901 to head b47967a659fd7e631ce24e41a26cd47437afc19c: a new stdlib-only probe script, the floor probe in python.py and tools.py, the CLI environment section and non-zero exit, the discover gate helper and its two call sites, and two new test files.
item_verdicts.done_when: the node done-when is tools status jt-60sa passing on the 3.12 recipe and failing naming the floor without it, plus the discover refusal; the retained live logs show both and the focused gate is 81 passed EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to extend the facility tool probe to report the facility remote_environment block's interpreter floor and per-module importability and to gate discover signals/code on an unmet floor; imas_codex/remote/tools.py:550 probe_remote_environment and imas_codex/remote/python.py:266 deliver it.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, gate uv run pytest tests/remote tests/cli/test_tools_status_environment.py 81 passed EXIT=0 at b47967a65, negative control red on the floor test, baseline_suite and after_suite both completed with failure_count 0.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the reviewed manifest's declared paths; git diff --name-only 887486007..b47967a659fd7e631ce24e41a26cd47437afc19c lists exactly the ten declared paths and nothing else.

justifications.durability: tests/remote/test_tools_environment.py and tests/cli/test_tools_status_environment.py assert the floor, module verdicts and the CLI exit, and the negative control reddens test_floor_is_the_blocks_not_the_global_minimum when the block floor is ignored.
justifications.evidence: /tmp/jt60sa-toolsenv-base.log records 66 passed EXIT=0, /tmp/jt60sa-toolsenv-tests.log 81 passed EXIT=0, and /tmp/jt60sa-toolsenv-negative.log reddens the floor test, but the landing fragment's base-arm revision and its live fail-mechanism narrative disagree with the retained logs.
justifications.fit: the change extends the existing owners, imas_codex/remote/python.py's floor primitive and imas_codex/remote/tools.py's check_all_tools and the existing tools status command, with one prober, though tools status now probes the environment twice.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_codex/remote/python.py:266 judges the block interpreter with PythonVersion.meets_minimum against the block floor and imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py:441 refuses a scan with the floor and the fix, matching plan section 6.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 887486007..b47967a65 lists the ten declared paths, with no dependency, schema or plan change and no new CLI command.
